constraints.description: A project that uses satellite-based earth observation, positioning, navigation or related timing data and services must use Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS. Other data and services may additionally be used.
Project results must contribute to all three stated expected outcomes. The binding is 'all', not 'one or more'.
The proposal earmarks resources for cooperation with existing in-situ data collection frameworks, named as GBIF, OBIS and LUCAS.

The project foresees sufficient means for effective coordination with projects selected under ESA's FuturEO programme. The topic sits in the biodiversity cluster of the EC-ESA Earth System Science Initiative.
Demonstration cases ensure interoperability with European and global frameworks, named as the Global Ecosystem Typology and EUNIS.

The project delivers FAIR data, harmonisation workflows and processing protocols, and links observation data to relevant data infrastructures, including EOSC, the European Common Data Spaces and SAGE where applicable.
Demonstration cases align with reporting requirements under the Habitats Directive, the Birds Directive, the Marine Strategy Framework Directive and the EU Nature Restoration Regulation.
The Joint Research Centre may join the consortium as a zero-funding beneficiary or as an associated partner and takes no part in preparing or submitting the proposal.

The Commission estimates that an EU contribution of around EUR 5.00 million per project is appropriate, within a total indicative topic budget of EUR 10.00 million funding about two projects. Requesting a different amount does not preclude submission or selection.
